packages.name: tico
packages.title: tico
packages.description: A customizable multi-system game launcher and emulator frontend.
packages.author: tico
packages.details:
tico is a Nintendo Switch game launcher and emulator frontend with support for multiple retro systems through independently maintained emulator cores.

It provides a customizable home interface, game-library browsing, cover and artwork management, RetroAchievements integration, touch support, and built-in management for supported emulator cores.

Additional emulator cores and supporting files can be installed or updated from within tico.
packages.changelog:
0.8.0

tico 0.8.0 is the biggest update yet. Emulators are now modules that install and update from the new tico Store, every account on your Switch gets its own tico, and every emulator has been rebuilt, with eight new ones. Your friends can see what you're playing on Discord, and your games can sit right on the Switch home menu.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Read [Upgrading to tico 0.8.0](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/182) before you update.** tico 0.8.0 comes with no emulators: install the ones you use from the Store after updating. The 3.0.0 emulators need tico 0.8.0, and tico 0.8.0 needs the 3.0.0 emulators. Most of your data moves by itself; back up `sdmc:/tico/saves/`, `sdmc:/tico/states/` and `sdmc:/tico/system/` first.

Full write-up on the forum: [What's new in tico 0.8.0](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/192).

## Highlights

- **Emulators are modules.** tico no longer has a built-in list of cores: each emulator installs from the Store, brings its own consoles and settings, and updates on its own.
- **The tico Store** replaces the core manager: emulators, apps, games, ports, soundpacks and console packs, from the official repository and any others you add, downloading in the background.
- **Every emulator rebuilt**, with a new quick menu, per-game settings, auto save and states with pictures. **Eight new emulators** bring the Nintendo 3DS (Dekopon), Nintendo DS, PlayStation 2, Virtual Boy, WonderSwan, Sega 32X, Atari 2600, MSX and ColecoVision.
- **Every account has its own tico**: look, sound, Home, saves, states, playtime and RetroAchievements belong to whoever is playing.
- **Several game folders, USB drives and NTFS**, and new games show up by themselves.
- **Discord Rich Presence**: the game you're playing, with its cover, on your Discord profile, in tico and outside it.
- **Forwarders**: put tico, or any of your games, on the Switch home menu.
- **Playtime that works**, counted per account by the emulators themselves.
- **Console packs**, a new lock screen, German and Russian, and a new logo.

---

## Emulators are modules now

Until now, tico carried a fixed list of cores and consoles, and every new emulator needed a new tico. Now each emulator is a module: a package you install from the Store that tells tico everything about itself.

- **Install only what you play.** Pick an emulator in the Store, and its consoles appear in Games straight away, without restarting tico. Remove it and they're gone.
- **Updates on their own schedule.** An emulator can be improved and released without waiting for a tico update, and the Store tells you when one is ready.
- **Each module brings what it needs**: its consoles and file types, its settings, which BIOS files it needs, its game lists, colors and artwork, and whether it supports achievements. Some add the console's own menu, like the Wii Menu, at the top of its games.
- **BIOS files per emulator**, in a folder named after it (`system/snes9x`, `system/dolphin`…). tico moves your existing files there for you, without overwriting anything.
- **Custom folders per emulator**: a Paths tab for its own ROMs, system, saves and states folders, including on USB drives.
- **Game Settings**: Settings › Emulator lists each emulator's games and lets you give any game its own settings. In the game list, the **+** menu's Game Settings goes straight there.
- **Open to everyone.** Modules are a documented format: see [Creating tico Modules](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/149) and [Creating a Store Repository](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/150).

The old core manager and the `sdmc:/tico/cores` folder are gone.

## Emulators

Every emulator was rebuilt on a shared frontend, so they look and work the same way. Unless noted, all of them get:

- A new quick menu (press **+** and **−** together), full settings and per-game settings. See [The In-Game Menu](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/186).
- Auto save and continue where you left off, and states with pictures.
- Button mapping, [cheats](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/180) and configurable fast forward.
- Zipped games, several ROM folders and USB drives.
- Per-account saves, states and playtime, and tico's own RetroAchievements sign-in.
- Most render with Vulkan and support [RetroArch slang shaders](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/181). Several have [frame generation](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/184).
- A tip when a game starts that **+** and **−** open the quick menu (Settings › General › Playing turns it off).

### New emulators

- **[Dekopon](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/196) (Nintendo 3DS)**: replaces Azahar. Faster 3DS emulation built for the Switch, with frame generation and fewer shader stutters. Your 3DS saves carry over: see [Mods and Texture Packs in tico Dekopon](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/179) and [Using Cheats with tico Dekopon](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/28).
- **[DraStic](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/167) (Nintendo DS)**: new screen layouts, a large-screen mode and screen overlays, cheats, auto save and per-game settings.
- **[NetherSX2](https://github.com/ticohq/tico-NetherSX2/releases/tag/3.0.0) (PlayStation 2)**: needs a game's full memory, so start tico through an installed title (hold **R**) or a forwarder.
- **[Beetle VB](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/198) (Virtual Boy)**: both D-pads on one controller, palettes and 3D modes.
- **[Beetle Cygne](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/199) (WonderSwan and WonderSwan Color)**: vertical games rotate the screen and the buttons with Select.
- **[PicoDrive](https://github.com/ticohq/tico-picodrive/releases/latest) (Sega 32X)**: the SH-2 dynamic recompiler running on the Switch, and the six-button pad.
- **[Stella](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/197) (Atari 2600)**: the console's switches on the controller, paddles on the left stick, palettes and phosphor.
- **[blueMSX](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/200) (MSX, MSX2, ColecoVision, Spectravideo and SC-3000)**: MSX cartridges work out of the box on the free C-BIOS, plus an on-screen keyboard.

### Updated emulators

- **[Dolphin](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/166) (GameCube and Wii)**: draws with deko3d. Shake, Tilt and Swing on any button, Gecko cheat downloads and Riivolution mods, online play via Wiimmfi and WiiLink, the Skylanders portal, WiiWare, Virtual Console, Triforce, the Wii Menu and the official GameCube adapter. Saves move to tico's saves folder. See [Dolphin: Mods, Texture Packs, Online Play and More](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/185).
- **[DuckStation](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/168) (PlayStation)**: a much newer DuckStation, with deko3D and Vulkan renderers, RetroArch shaders and frame generation. Change Disc, with disc 2 reading disc 1's save, and more disc formats.
- **[PPSSPP](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/176) (PSP)**: PPSSPP's latest development version. Network multiplayer, frame generation, the right stick as the D-pad, and a clock that follows your time zone.
- **[Flycast](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/171) (Dreamcast, NAOMI and Atomiswave)**: based on Flycast 2.7, with shaders, frame generation, Change Disc, vibration and upright vertical arcade games.
- **[YabaSanshiro](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/178) (Saturn)**: updated to 1.20.46, with OpenGL or Vulkan, AMD FSR upscaling, frame generation, Change Disc, multitap, cartridges and a BIOS per region.
- **[Mupen64Plus](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/175) (Nintendo 64)**: rebuilt on GLideN64, with internal resolution, widescreen, large romhacks, and saves written while you play.
- **[Snes9x](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/177) (SNES)**: Vulkan and shaders. PAL games run at the right speed, and games with a clock keep their time.
- **[FCEUmm](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/170) (NES)**: Vulkan, shaders and HD texture packs. PAL games run at the right speed, and Famicom Disk System games get achievements.
- **[Gambatte](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/172) (Game Boy and Color)**: Vulkan and shaders, and games with a clock keep their time.
- **[mGBA](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/174) (Game Boy Advance)**: joins the shared frontend, with Vulkan, shaders, motion sensors and vibration.
- **[Genesis Plus GX](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/173) (Mega Drive, Master System, Game Gear, SG-1000 and Sega CD)**: Vulkan and shaders, plus Change Disc for Sega CD.
- **[FinalBurn Neo](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/169) (Arcade)**: Vulkan, shaders, upright vertical games and smoother frame pacing.

Also new for emulators: Dolphin loads games faster, shader caches live in each emulator's folder instead of `sdmc:/.mesa`, PPSSPP's overlay follows tico's theme, frame generation reads one `Lossless.dll` shared by every emulator (`sdmc:/tico/system/lsfg/`), and RetroAchievements now covers Game Gear, Master System and Sega CD.

> [!NOTE]
> **Dolphin and Dekopon no longer overclock the console by themselves.** Boost mode (CPU 1785 MHz, GPU 768 MHz) is still there as an option, off by default: Dekopon's is in Settings › General › Performance, Dolphin's in its settings. Dolphin only boosts briefly while a game loads (*Boost while loading the game*, which you can turn off). We recommend setting your clocks with your own overclocking tool, such as sys-clk, sys-clk-OC or Horizon-OC, instead.

---

## Every account has its own tico

- Each Switch account keeps its own look, sound, Home layout, accounts and RetroAchievements sign-in.
- Saves, states and playtime are kept per account. A one-time welcome wizard moves your existing settings, saves and states to the account that has been playing.
- A new lock screen in tico's colors picks who's playing. It works even with a single user.
- Settings › General › Starting tico: select the user at start, or always start with a user you choose.
- Settings › General › Saves and states shows your account's folders by your name, and each account's folder on the SD card has a file named after the account, so you can tell them apart on a computer.
- Your settings are kept in one sealed file. Emulators only receive what they need, like a RetroAchievements token, never your password.

See [Accounts, Saves and the Lock Screen](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/183).

## The tico Store

### Browsing

- Search, Discover, Apps, Games, Ports, Soundpacks, Console Packs, Installed and Sources, in a sidebar.
- Discover has a featured carousel and Updates and New shelves. Games and Ports have a shelf per console.
- View all opens a console's full list, with a letter rail (ZL/ZR jump between letters), search inside the list, sorting by name or size, and a switch for betas and demos.
- A game's regions and revisions show as one entry, with your console's region first.
- A game's page says which emulator plays it, and **Y** installs that emulator if you don't have it.
- Search remembers your last five searches and groups results by category.

### Downloading and installing

- A Downloads tab: packages download in the background while you use tico. The queue pauses while you play and resumes later.
- Installed lists updates first. **Y** updates everything, including tico itself.
- Choose where packages install (Settings › Store), and uninstalling removes exactly what a package installed.
- Every file is checked before it's written, and large packages stream straight to disk.

### Repositories and torrents

- Add any repository. Trusted and verified ones are marked, and only they can feature packages or ship emulators, unless you allow it in Settings › Store.
- Packages can come from torrents: through TorBox, Real-Debrid, AllDebrid or your own TorrServer, through tico-fetch in the background, or with tico's own engine, now much faster, with uploads, encryption and uTP.
- The Store, RetroAchievements and SteamGridDB keep working when the Switch's DNS fails.

## Discord Rich Presence

Your friends see what you're doing on your Switch: the game, its cover, the console and how long you've been playing, or where you are in tico when you're not in a game.

- Install it from Settings › Accounts › Discord. It ships inside tico, so there's nothing to download.
- Log in by scanning a QR code with your phone. tico uses its own Discord app, which only asks to set your activity and see your name.
- It's off until you turn it on, and you choose what shows: activity outside tico, the screen you're on, core names, and your tico language.
- Switch games, forwarders and other homebrew outside tico show with their icon too: the eShop's, tinfoil's, or the app's own.
- Your login is sealed on the SD card and is never stored as plain text.

See [Discord Rich Presence in tico](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/190).

## Forwarders

Put tico, or any of your games, on the Switch home menu.

- **Install tico Forwarder on Switch Home** (Settings › General › Forwarders) puts tico on the home menu as a full application, with all of the console's memory.
- **Create Forwarder**, in a game's quick menu (**+**), puts that game on the home menu with its cover as the icon. Pick who plays it: a user of your choice, or the Switch's own user picker. The game opens straight away with that player's saves, settings and accounts, and quitting it takes you back to the home menu.
- Forwarders get the 3 CPU cores a game gets. Turn on Ask CPU Cores on Install to choose 4 when you install one.

> [!WARNING]
> Forwarders are off by default. They're unofficial applications, and a console that goes online with them installed on sysMMC risks a ban from Nintendo's online services. Use them on emuMMC, keep the console away from Nintendo's servers with 90DNS (or Atmosphère's DNS MITM), and consider Incognito (back up PRODINFO first). tico explains this and asks you to confirm before it lets you create one.

## Your library

- Several game folders per console: tico's ROMs folder first, then the ones you add.
- USB drives formatted as FAT, exFAT or NTFS (read-only). Folders on a drive are remembered even when its mount name changes, and plugging a drive in or out rescans the consoles that use it.
- Library watching: games added to or removed from your folders appear without a rescan.
- Game lists load 3–6× faster with about half the memory, read straight from DAT files (No-Intro, Redump, TOSEC, arcade).
- Disc games in `.chd`, `.iso` or `.m3u` get their real title and cover. Consoles without a game list simply list their files. See [Supported ROM Formats](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/17) and the [BIOS Setup Guide](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/18).

## Playing

- Playtime: emulators count the time they actually play, each account keeps its own log, and game cards show the totals.
- Change Disc in the quick menu for multi-disc games.
- Launches show the game's artwork, then "Fetching achievements" while badges download, then fade into the game.
- tico signs in to RetroAchievements and fetches badges itself.

## Console packs

A console pack swaps your consoles' covers, backgrounds, logos, symbols and colors in one go. Find them in the Store's Console Packs tab, and pick one in Settings › Interface › Card settings › Console Pack. See [Using Console Packs](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/187).

## Settings, navigation and languages

- German and Russian, and every other translation updated.
- General is in sections, and the Store has its own settings category.
- Font Scale in Display, and Startup Screen, Navigation Type and Game Splash in Interface.
- Two-finger swipes move between Home, Games, Trophies and Store. Swipe up from the bottom edge for the dock.
- Faster start-up, and covers decoded at the size they're drawn.
- A new tico logo, on the home menu and in the Homebrew Menu.

## Fixes

- Quitting or launching a game no longer hangs on a black screen.
- Fixed crashes at start-up, when leaving a game after its first session, when closing tico mid-download, and the "2162-0002" crash when starting a fourth game in a row.
- Fixed tico freezing after installing an emulator from the Store.
- File names that aren't UTF-8 no longer crash tico.
- Changing a Home card's size keeps editing the same card.
- Updating an emulator no longer fails with "could not be written to the SD card".
- Saturn no longer shows "Game List Not Found" when its emulator ships a list.
- The Store's product page sidebar responds to taps, and the torrent service settings can be reached again.

---

## Breaking changes since 0.7.9

Everything below is in [Upgrading to tico 0.8.0](https://forum.ticoverse.com/topic/182), with what to do:

- **No built-in emulators**: install the ones you use from the Store. `sdmc:/tico/cores/` is removed.
- **Saves and states per account**: `sdmc:/tico/saves/users/<account>/<console>/` and `sdmc:/tico/states/users/<account>/<console>/`. The welcome wizard moves them to the account you pick.
- **BIOS folders per emulator**: `system/<console>/` becomes `system/<emulator>/`, moved by tico.
- **3DS**: Dekopon replaces Azahar. Your saves, updates and DLC carry over; mods, texture packs and cheats from tico Azahar need moving once.
- **Dolphin** saves move from its own folder to tico's saves folder, and `.chd` games are no longer listed (convert them to RVZ or ISO).
- **Settings are sealed**: tico's `.jsonc` files in `sdmc:/tico/config/` move into `sdmc:/tico/data/tico.vault`, so editing them by hand no longer works.
- **Save names**: Snes9x, FCEUmm, Gambatte, mGBA and FinalBurn Neo name saves `<game>.srm`; older `.sav` files are renamed by themselves.
- **No automatic overclock**: Dolphin and Dekopon no longer raise the clocks for the whole game. Boost mode is an option you can turn on, off by default; we recommend your own overclocking tool (sys-clk, sys-clk-OC or Horizon-OC) instead.

## Installing

Copy `tico.nro` to `sdmc:/switch/tico/` (over the old one) and start it from the Homebrew Menu. Then open the Store and install your emulators.

## Want to Contribute?

Every emulator has its own repository under the **tico GitHub organization**, making development, issue tracking and contributions easier.

Bug reports, feature requests and pull requests are always welcome. Please respect each emulator's original license and attribution requirements.

Found something odd, or have an idea? Post it in the [forum](https://forum.ticoverse.com). Thank you for playing with tico!

packages.name: prelude
packages.title: Prelude
packages.description: Switch between Nextendo Network and Nintendo's official network services.
packages.author: Nextendo Network
packages.details:
Prelude is a Nintendo Switch homebrew application for switching an Atmosphere console between Nextendo Network and Nintendo's official network services.

Nextendo mode configures the Atmosphere files and patches needed to connect supported games and services to Nextendo Network. Nintendo mode removes Prelude's changes and restores the console's normal Nintendo network configuration.

Prelude applies its changes through files and settings that Atmosphere reads at boot, making the process reversible. After selecting a network mode, the console reboots so the new configuration can take effect.
packages.changelog:
v4.0.7

## What's Changed
* Online-play invitations: Prelude now redirects the system invitation service (`app.lp1.five.nintendo.net`) to Nextendo. Inviting a friend from a game no longer fails with error 2121-2906, and invitations work Switch to Switch and between Switch and Ryujinx/Citron.
* Build: the bundled network_mitm sysmodule is now checked against a pinned SHA-256 at build time.

Update in-app from Prelude (press Y on the update banner), or copy `nextendo.nro` to `/switch/` on your SD card.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/NextendoNetwork/Prelude-Nextendo/compare/v4.0.6...v4.0.7


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/NextendoNetwork/Prelude-Nextendo/compare/v4.0.6...v4.0.7

packages.name: pipensx
packages.title: pipensx
packages.description: Download and install supported content with direct torrent or debrid backends.
packages.author: i3sey
packages.details:
pipensx is a Nintendo Switch download manager and streaming package installer with support for direct BitTorrent and optional debrid providers including TorBox, Real-Debrid, AllDebrid, and TorrServer.

For debrid-only use, leave Direct BitTorrent disabled and configure a supported debrid provider. In that mode, pipensx can route downloads through the debrid service instead of joining the torrent swarm from the Switch.

The application also includes a persistent download queue, pause/resume and recovery support, catalog browsing, network diagnostics, and installation support for compatible packages.
packages.changelog:
1.6.4

## What's new in 1.6.4 (compared to 1.6.3)

**In short:** eliminated Horizon OS FS hangs and Atmosphère NCM panics during large game installs; preserved file selection access on completed downloads for grabbing extra DLCs, patches, and translations; dynamic NRO relocation and robust in-app updating; reliable Switch port deployment; fixed catalog sorting and repack classification.

### Installation & Storage Stability (Critical)

- **Upfront NCM placeholder allocation (`a69240e`):** reverted dynamic 256 MiB placeholder chunk resizing (`ncmContentStorageSetPlaceHolderSize`) back to standard upfront full-size placeholder creation (`ncmContentStorageCreatePlaceHolder`). On FAT32 SD cards, mid-stream placeholder resizing caused heavy SDMMC bus lockups, deadlocking Horizon OS FS and triggering an unrecoverable `std::abort()` panic in Atmosphère's NCM sysmodule (`0100000000000002`). This also resolves issues with 4GB+ NCA split files (`CreateOption_BigFile`).
- **Filesystem directory creation fix (`b45895d`):** normalized `mkdirs` across install and download pipelines to strip the device mount prefix (`sdmc:/`) and trailing slashes, preventing failed `mkdir` calls under libnx.

### Downloads & File Management

- **File selection for existing & completed tasks (`ee204d3`):** kept the "Select files" button accessible on the game detail card even when a release is already active or finished, replacing redundant "View download" links.
- **Incremental file downloads:** opening file selection on an existing task pre-populates previous choices, allowing users to effortlessly select and download additional DLCs, voiceovers, or community translations without deleting existing completed downloads.
- **Fast-path metainfo reuse:** opening file selection immediately reads cached metainfo without waiting for redundant network re-announces.

### In-App Updater & Path Relocation

- **Dynamic NRO relocation (`b66d441`):** resolved the active executable path from `argv[0]`, ensuring smooth in-app updates even if the NRO binary was renamed or placed in non-standard SD card locations.
- **Duplicate NRO cleanup & sync:** cleanly updates the running binary, synchronizing duplicates and removing orphaned intermediate files on the SD card.
- **In-app update notifications restored:** restored reliable update checking in Settings and accurate update prompt banners.

### Ports & Deployments

- **Direct Switch port deployment (`b45895d`):** enabled starting PortInstall tasks with manual approval from `SwitchDeployPreviewActivity` directly on the console without requiring web panel rule triggers.
- **Deployment UX improvements:** prevented duplicate actions during in-flight port operations and surfaced detailed error messages on deployment failures.

### Catalog & Classification

- **Repack & full game classification (`caf624a`):** classified full game repacks and multi-content bundles under the Games tab rather than misidentifying them as standalone updates.
- **MIG Switch & media routing:** routed MIG Switch (.xci/.xcz) and media assets to the Ports / Archives section with sanitized package types.
- **Catalog sorting regression fix (`5da20cf`):** restored proper release date and name sorting across catalog views.
- **Updated catalog snapshot:** refreshed bundled offline catalog data.

packages.name: status-monitor-deux
packages.title: Status Monitor Deux
packages.description: Monitor Nintendo Switch hardware statistics in real time.
packages.author: masagrator
packages.details:
Status Monitor Deux is the next generation of Status Monitor Overlay for Nintendo Switch.

It displays real-time hardware statistics such as per-core CPU usage, GPU load, CPU/GPU/RAM frequencies, memory usage, temperatures, and fan behavior through an overlay interface.

Unlike the original Status Monitor Overlay, Status Monitor Deux uses customizable `.smd` script files for its display modes and `.smse` extension files for additional services, giving you much more control over how information is presented.

Its configuration, modes, extensions, and localization files are stored under `sd:/config/status-monitor-deux`.

packages.name: missioncontrol
packages.title: MissionControl
packages.description: Use controllers from other consoles via Bluetooth.
packages.author: ndeadly
packages.details:
Use controllers from other consoles natively on your Nintendo Switch via Bluetooth. No dongles or other external hardware necessary.

After installing this package, reboot your console to activate the module.

MissionControl supports a wide range of Bluetooth controllers, including Wii/Wii U, DualShock 3/4, DualSense, Xbox One Bluetooth controllers, several 8BitDo models, and many third-party controllers. It integrates with the Switch's native controller pairing and remapping interfaces, supports rumble and motion controls on compatible devices, and can connect multiple non-Switch Bluetooth controllers simultaneously.
packages.changelog:
v0.16.0

This release adds support for firmware 23.0.0/23.0.1, adds a new setting for Dualsense adaptive trigger travel distance and fixes several outstanding issues. See below for full changelog. _Note: the codebase has undergone some non-trivial refactoring since the previous release. While most of the changes shouldn't result in any noticable differences to the end user, there is the possibility that new issues have been introduced into code that was previously stable. I tried to get users in my discord server to help test to ensure the new release was as bug free as possible, but was met with a rather underwhelming response. Since I can't hold up the release for 23.0.0 indefinitely I am releasing in its current state. Please look out for and report any regressions you may come across, and if you value timely and stable future releases, consider subscribing to notifications in the #testing channel of my discord server and helping out._ New users landing on this release page should first check out the readme on the [main project page](https://github.com/ndeadly/MissionControl#readme) for the official project documentation. There you can find installation and usage instructions along with an FAQ section that will answer most of your questions. ### Changelog - Added full support for firmware 23.0.0/23.0.1 - Added a feature for setting the maximum travel distance of Dualsense adaptive triggers - Modified device class check patch to allow JoyconDroid (non-root) to accept a broader range of devices - Reworked battery level reporting for Sony controllers to be more accurate and avoid warning notifications when the level is not critically low - Added mitm for shortened versions of btm GetDeviceCondition and GetDeviceInfo functions - Fixed a bug where the priority of the bluetooth event mitm thread was lower than it should have been - Miscellaneous internal changes to improve accuracy and coverage of controller protocol implementation

packages.name: lockpick-rcm
packages.title: Lockpick_RCM
packages.description: Extract Nintendo Switch encryption keys from the boot environment.
packages.author: shchmue, impeeza
packages.details:
Lockpick_RCM is a bare-metal Nintendo Switch payload used to derive and dump encryption keys without booting Horizon OS.

This package uses the Hekate-compatible release and installs the included files to their intended SD card locations so Lockpick_RCM can be launched through Hekate's payload menu.

Generated keys are saved to `sd:/switch/prod.keys` and, when available, `sd:/switch/title.keys`.

packages.name: sys-dock
packages.title: sys-dock
packages.description: Enable higher docked display bandwidth and refresh rates.
packages.author: masagrator
packages.details:
sys-dock is a Nintendo Switch sysmodule that patches docked DisplayPort link training to allow higher-bandwidth display modes and higher refresh rates.

It is primarily intended for use alongside FPSLocker, especially on OLED models where the default docked DisplayPort configuration can limit available refresh rates. The included overlay lets you enable or disable individual DisplayPort patches and see which patches are currently active.

Configuration is stored in `sd:/config/sys-dock/config.ini` and can be edited manually or through the overlay.

Because sys-dock changes low-level dock and display behavior, incompatible docks, displays, cables, or patch combinations may cause display corruption, instability, or other unexpected behavior.
packages.changelog:

- Introduce a patch `force_full_render_pass` that solves an issue some people had with glitched horizontal lines while using high refresh rate at 1080p. Confirmed with OLED, V2 and V1.
  - Removed redocking feature, use this patch instead.

packages.name: sys-patch
packages.title: sys-patch
packages.description: Apply system patches automatically at boot.
packages.author: btc08gh, impeeza
packages.details:
sys-patch is a Nintendo Switch sysmodule that automatically applies fs, es, ldr, nifm, and nim patches when the system boots.

It can patch both sysMMC and emuMMC and includes an overlay for changing configuration options and checking which patches were successfully applied. The overlay distinguishes between patches applied by sys-patch and patches that were already present from another source.

Configuration is stored in `sd:/config/sys-patch/config.ini`, where you can control sysMMC and emuMMC patching, logging, and version-pattern behavior.

Because sys-patch modifies low-level system behavior, it is best suited for advanced users who understand Atmosphere and firmware compatibility.

packages.name: edizon-overlay
packages.title: EdiZon-Overlay
packages.description: Toggle cheats in a convenient overlay.
packages.author: WerWolv, proferabg, ppkantorski
packages.details:
EdiZon-Overlay provides in-game cheat management through the Ultrahand overlay environment.

It allows you to browse and toggle cheats for the currently running title without leaving the game. This maintained fork continues the original EdiZon-Overlay by WerWolv and includes support for newer Horizon OS and libultrahand releases.

The overlay also supports cheat submenus and optional cheats that are enabled automatically whenever the overlay is opened.

packages.name: saltynx
packages.title: SaltyNX
packages.description: Background process for the Nintendo Switch for file/code modification.
packages.author: shinyquagsire23, masagrator
packages.details:
SaltyNX is a background process for Nintendo Switch that enables runtime file and code modification in retail games.

Originally created by shinyquagsire23 and maintained as an expanded fork by masagrator, SaltyNX provides the underlying framework used by tools such as FPSLocker and other game-modification plugins.

This fork includes numerous quality-of-life, compatibility, performance-monitoring, display-control, and plugin-injection improvements.

packages.name: sysdvr
packages.title: SysDVR
packages.description: Stream Nintendo Switch gameplay over USB or network.
packages.author: exelix11
packages.details:
SysDVR is a Nintendo Switch sysmodule for streaming gameplay capture over USB or a local network.

The full SysDVR package supports both network and USB streaming and includes the SysDVR Settings homebrew application for changing streaming modes and configuration.

SysDVR runs in the background as an Atmosphere sysmodule and can be started or stopped when needed to reduce sysmodule memory usage.

packages.name: sys-con
packages.title: sys-con
packages.description: Use USB controllers from other consoles on Nintendo Switch.
packages.author: cathery, o0Zz
packages.details:
sys-con is a Nintendo Switch sysmodule that adds support for third-party USB controllers.

It supports a wide range of HID and XInput-compatible gamepads, including PlayStation, Xbox, PC controllers, arcade sticks, wheels, and other USB input devices. Controllers can be used in docked mode or through a compatible USB-C OTG adapter in handheld mode.

Configuration files under `sd:/config/sys-con/` allow you to customize button mappings, stick and trigger behavior, deadzones, polling settings, controller profiles, and other device-specific options.

packages.name: emuiibo
packages.title: emuiibo
packages.description: Virtual amiibo emulation system for Nintendo Switch.
packages.author: XorTroll
packages.details:
Virtual amiibo (amiibo emulation) system for Nintendo Switch.

Virtual amiibos are stored under `sd:/emuiibo/amiibo` and should be organized into subdirectories. emuiibo intercepts the Switch's amiibo services, allowing compatible games to use virtual amiibos through its overlay.

Use the emuiibo overlay to enable or disable amiibo emulation, select an active virtual amiibo, connect or disconnect it, and configure options such as randomized UUIDs.

packages.name: sysdvr-patches
packages.title: SysDVR Patches
packages.description: Enable SysDVR recording support in more games.
packages.author: exelix11
packages.details:
SysDVR Patches contains firmware-specific Atmosphere ExeFS patches that relax Nintendo Switch recording restrictions for use with SysDVR.

The patches make more games behave as if recording is enabled, remove several capture restrictions, and help prevent crashes when recording-memory allocation fails.

These patches are tied to specific firmware versions. Installing patches intended for a different firmware may cause crashes or prevent affected system modules from loading.

packages.details:
90DNS Tester checks network connectivity from your Nintendo Switch to determine whether Nintendo services are being successfully blocked.

packages.name: nx-fancontrol
packages.title: NX-FanControl
packages.description: Custom fan curve control for Nintendo Switch.
packages.author: Zathawo, dominatorul
packages.details:
NX-FanControl is a Nintendo Switch sysmodule and overlay for customizing the console's internal fan curve.

It allows you to define multiple temperature points with corresponding fan speeds, giving you more control over the balance between cooling performance and fan noise. The overlay also provides real-time monitoring of SoC temperature and fan RPM.

Because NX-FanControl directly changes fan behavior, use sensible fan curves and avoid settings that significantly reduce cooling at high temperatures.
packages.changelog:
1.0.5+

Added

Support for 10 fan curve points, giving finer control over fan behavior.
SoC temperature and Fan Speed readings in the overlay.

Changed

Removed fan level change threshold — Fan speed now updates every cycle, giving immediate response to temperature or setting changes.

~Reduced sleep time from 500ms to 250ms — Updates 4 times per second, providing a more responsive experience while staying efficient.~

Optimized sleep state checking — System sleep is now checked every 20 iterations (~5 seconds) instead of every loop, reducing overhead while keeping power-saving functionality.

Fixed

Various minor bug fixes for improved stability and reliability.

Recompiled for latest Atmosphere support

2/13/2026

Reduced heap size from 512kb to 50kb. Now it uses 10x less memory.
Reduced sleep time to 50 ms and for temps over 50 degrees to 25ms.
Fixed critical config corruption bug: corrected fwrite/fread parameter order so fan curves now save/load properly.
Fixed fan speed not updating due to hysteresis logic: fan now updates immediately.
Removed unused variables causing Werror build failures.

packages.name: sys-tune
packages.title: sys-tune
packages.description: Background audio player for Nintendo Switch.
packages.author: HookedBehemoth, ppkantorski
packages.details:
sys-tune is a background audio player for Nintendo Switch with an Ultrahand overlay for controlling playback.

It supports MP3, FLAC, and WAV audio, playlist browsing, seeking, shuffle and repeat modes, persistent playback settings, per-title behavior, and separate control over music and game audio volume.

Music can be played from the SD card and managed without leaving the currently running game or application. sys-tune can also be configured for HOME Menu background music and title-specific playback behavior.

Because audio playback can interfere with sleep mode or titles that heavily use the system audio renderer, pause playback or stop the service if you encounter audio or sleep-related issues.

packages.name: ldn-mitm
packages.title: ldn_mitm
packages.description: Play local-wireless Nintendo Switch games over LAN.
packages.author: spacemeowx2, DefenderOfHyrule
packages.details:
ldn_mitm is an Atmosphere sysmodule that replaces the Nintendo Switch ldn service and redirects local-wireless discovery over LAN networking.

It allows games that normally communicate through local wireless to work over a network connection, and is commonly used together with switch-lan-play for online play with supported local-wireless titles.

The package also includes configuration tools and should be rebooted after installation so the sysmodule can start.
